note: Pre-registered hypotheses that have NO primary source behind them (docs/v3.3/RESEARCH-PACKAGING.md §10). They are recorded here, before any data exists, so that a result can be judged honestly and a new hypothesis never silently replaces one of these. They are NOT experiment-engine specs (they use different variables and mostly need 16:9 long-form, which can be A/B tested, or a retention curve), so they are kept separate from the paired `spec.json` experiments.
rule: judged by WATCH TIME (YouTube's own A/B metric, support.google.com/youtube/answer/16391400), never by CTR; no threshold is adopted before the data exists

experiments.hypothesis: A coloured on-screen callout ("sticker") on the cover changes performance.
experiments.minimum: 16:9 long-form only; Shorts cannot be A/B tested natively and a before/after comparison confounds topic
experiments.decision_rule: not set yet — record the pair of matched videos (sticker vs no sticker) and read the watch-time share once both have 14 days of data

experiments.hypothesis: A mid-video visual CTA (no spoken words) at ~50 % costs more retention than it gains in conversions.
experiments.minimum: matched pairs, one arm with the on-screen CTA and one without, same narrator and structure
experiments.decision_rule: not set yet — a drop in the retention curve at the CTA's timestamp decides it

experiments.hypothesis: Sentence-case titles reach more viewers than title-case (or the reverse).
experiments.minimum: the same videos' 3 title variants through Studio Test & compare (only long-form is eligible)
experiments.decision_rule: not set yet — Studio picks the winner by watch time over ~2 weeks
